content:
Owen Phillips: got a user question that keeps popping up in evals/support: when streaming tool calls, they see `arguments` look "truncated" (e.g. `{\"q\": \"foo`), then their code tries `JSON.parse` and blows up. what’s the right pattern here? also: do we guarantee args come in a single chunk ever?

Wei Chen: yeah we should be clearer in docs that args can be split across multiple deltas. you should only parse after you’ve received the *completed* tool call (or end-of-stream). if you parse on each delta you’ll get invalid JSON a bunch.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. canonical mental model for streaming tool calls:
- treat tool call `arguments` as a byte/string stream
- append deltas until tool call is marked complete
- then validate + parse once, call tool, and send a tool-result message back

Ibrahim Khan: for the examples we’re standardizing on:
1) accumulate partial tool args by `tool_call_id`
2) don’t assume args are valid JSON until the final tool-call event
3) same for structured output: don’t `json.loads` mid-stream

Ibrahim Khan: pseudo-code (language-agnostic):
```
state.tool_args[tool_call_id] += event.delta.arguments

if event.type == "response.tool_call.completed":
  raw = state.tool_args[tool_call_id]
  args = JSON.parse(raw)          # (with try/catch + error message)
  result = run_tool(event.name, args)
  client.responses.create({
    input: [
      { role: "assistant", tool_calls: [{ id: tool_call_id, name: event.name, arguments: raw }] },
      { role: "tool", tool_call_id, content: JSON.stringify(result) }
    ]
  })
```

Owen Phillips: ok so we should explicitly say: args are allowed to arrive fragmented; users must join deltas, then parse. and if the stream drops mid-args, they should retry from last completed item vs trying to salvage partial?

Ibrahim Khan: yep. if the stream disconnects mid-tool-args, you have two safe options:
- retry the request (idempotency key if you have one), or
- fall back to non-streaming for that call if your app can tolerate it
but don’t execute a tool from partial args.

Dana Lo: TS angle: we’ve seen people do `JSON.parse(evt.toolCall.arguments)` on `delta` events. should be more like:
```
const buf = new Map<string, string>();
for await (const evt of stream) {
  if (evt.type === 'response.tool_call.delta') {
    buf.set(evt.tool_call_id, (buf.get(evt.tool_call_id) ?? '') + (evt.delta.arguments ?? ''));
  }
  if (evt.type === 'response.tool_call.completed') {
    const raw = buf.get(evt.tool_call_id) ?? '';
    const args = JSON.parse(raw);
    ...
  }
}
```
(this is what we’re moving the docs + examples to)

Mateusz Zielinski: Go version is same story: keep a `map[string]strings.Builder` keyed by toolCallID. only unmarshal on the completed event. we also log the raw args on parse failure so support can see if it was a disconnect vs model emitted invalid JSON.

Wei Chen: I’m going to add a short callout box to the tool-calling streaming section: “Tool arguments may be emitted incrementally; only parse after completion.” This is the exact confusion we’re seeing in SUP-18421 / SUP-18436.

Elliot Price: docs tweak is in review now. linking the new runnable example here so we can just point folks at it next time: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/tree/main/streaming/tool-calls|redwood-examples: streaming tool calls (delta assembly + tool-result loop)>

Owen Phillips: perfect. I’ll paste that link in the help reply thread next time + note “don’t parse mid-stream”. thanks all. :thumbsup:

Dana Lo: also worth noting (for anyone answering users): if they’re doing “structured output” (JSON schema) while streaming, same pitfall—collect full text then validate, or use an incremental parser that can handle incomplete JSON. our docs should steer people to “collect then validate” as default.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. and we should keep terminology consistent: “delta events” vs “final/completed event”. I’ll drop this in the parity checklist too.

Wei Chen: added to the doc draft. will post the final URL once it’s live.
